chapter: Arriving in New York and founding the Afro-Cubans
title: Mario's concept: a new sound with jazz-level intonation
summary: Machito says their style had better phrasing and intonation because Mario had perfect pitch and wrote only what each musician could play.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Okay. At that time, did you have any idea about revolutionizing music, with the new sound that came from the Machito orchestra? Was that in your mind?

Yes, yes, because the sound I recorded with everyone. Our style was completely different, better interpretation, better phrasing. The intonation was fantastic because Mario he had a perfect pitch, so he knew how to tune the band. He knows the limitation of the musician.

What I am driving at is that here you had a lot of bands around that time. Macho, when you and Mario started your band you had, ahh, Caney, you had Montecino, La Siboney and a few others that escape my mind......

Noro Morales, yet they didn't have something, that jazz feeling which later rose to, you know, really overwhelmed everybody in the forties and that...... Did you and Mario had that in mind or did this come by accident when you heard the music interpreted by these musicians?

No, no, no, no, no. Mario is a is an architect. He knew all the limitations of the musicians that he had, so he had that particular way to say to the arranger, "Listen to the band, I don't want no experiment, I want everything that is written in that piece of paper that everybody is capable to play."
